title: Patterns & Sequences
sub: Adding, multiplying, and growing patterns; the nth term

steps.html:
Patterns & Sequences

+ the same8, 17, 26, 35 (+9)
× the same3, 9, 27, 81 (×3)
growing gaps5, 6, 8, 11, 15 (+1, +2, +3, +4)
say: Today: number patterns. Always look at the gaps between numbers first.
Some add the same amount each time. Eight, seventeen, twenty-six: plus nine.
Some multiply by the same amount. Three, nine, twenty-seven: times three.
And some have gaps that grow. Plus one, plus two, plus three, plus four. The next is twenty.

steps.html:
Jumping far ahead: the nth term

8, 17, 26, 35, …  25th term?
start 8, add 9 each time
25th term = 8 + 9 × 24 (24 jumps, not 25!)
= 8 + 216 = 224
say: What if they ask for the twenty-fifth term? Don't write them all out.
It starts at eight and adds nine each time.
To get to the twenty-fifth term, you make twenty-four jumps, not twenty-five. Like fence posts.
Eight plus nine times twenty-four is two twenty-four.
What's the twentieth term of four, seven, ten, thirteen?
steps.okSay: Yes! Four plus three times nineteen is sixty-one.
steps.noSay: Not quite. It starts at four and adds three. To reach the twentieth term you make nineteen jumps: four plus fifty-seven is sixty-one.

say: What's the next number? Two, six, eighteen, fifty-four.
steps.no: Gaps are 4, 12, 36, not the same. Ratios: × 3 each time. 54 × 3 = 162.
steps.noSay: Not quite. The gaps aren't equal, so check multiplying: each number is three times the one before. Fifty-four times three is one sixty-two.

say: Great! Now 4 practice questions. You'll see the answer and an explanation after each one.
Last part: three checkpoint questions. Get two out of three to finish the lesson. You've got this!

steps.html:
Remember

1. Look at the gaps first: same gap → adding.

2. Gaps growing fast → try multiplying.

3. nth term = start + gap × (n − 1).
say: Let's review. Look at the gaps first. Same gap means you're adding.
If the gaps grow fast, try multiplying.
And the nth term is the start plus the gap times n minus one. Great job!
